title: torchnpu-pinned-host-memory-lifecycle
summary: Diagnose TorchNPU pinned-host RAM allocation, asynchronous-copy lifetime, reuse and cache controls, then propose version-gated host-allocator changes. Use for pin_memory pressure or host allocation stalls, not device HBM or network transport.

applicability.scope: Diagnose TorchNPU pinned-host RAM allocation, asynchronous-copy ownership/readiness, reuse and path-specific cache controls.
applicability.input_contract: Installed versions/settings, host pressure and allocation/reuse distribution, stream timeline, owned versus registered/pageable buffers, selected host allocator path and host statistics/allocation timings.
applicability.produced_artifact: An ownership classification, source evidence IDs, one eligible allocator proposal, benefit/resource cost and rollback criteria for a later fresh-process comparison.
applicability.refusal_point: Keep baseline settings for live-buffer growth, pageable copies, stable reuse, unverified versions or unsupported paths; stop tuning on event/runtime errors and escalate external ownership or gate conflicts.

recommendations: Do not mutate an H2D source or read a D2H destination before completion; non_blocking=True alone proves neither overlap nor external-buffer lifetime tracking.

Interpret host allocated/active bytes using the selected host path, and test round/cache controls only in supported default-path fresh processes; a per-buffer cache threshold is not a total-cache cap.
Keep host and device allocator options separate and use an explicit quiescent boundary for host cache release; cache clearing is not a copy-completion barrier.
